description: This bar chart illustrates the relationship between percentage of parameters pruned and perplexity for two different pruning methods, “Per-Output” and “Per-Layer”. The horizontal axis represents the percentage of parameters pruned, labeled from 10% to 80% in 10% increments, and is a categorical axis. The vertical axis represents perplexity, labeled with a logarithmic scale ranging from 10⁰ to 10³, with tick labels at 10⁰, 10¹, 10², and 10³. Two bars are displayed for each percentage of parameters pruned: a blue bar representing “Per-Output” and an orange bar representing “Per-Layer”. For 10% pruning, the “Per-Output” bar has a height of approximately 5, while the “Per-Layer” bar has a height of approximately 4. At 80% pruning, the “Per-Output” bar reaches a height of approximately 950, and the “Per-Layer” bar reaches a height of approximately 1800. The bars are arranged in ascending order based on the percentage of parameters pruned. No bars are visually emphasized with shading, bolding, outlining, or annotations.
